correctness.rationale: The repaired Hilbert factorization holds in the full real spaces for every injection, including a possible f(a)=0 and the empty word. Prefixes 0^a have disjoint nonempty derivative supports D_a: a common suffix fixes its count of zeros r and then forces a=a' by injectivity. If a prefix already contains a one, a nonzero derivative is supported at precisely one all-ones suffix; the other prefixes have zero columns. Grouping coefficients by these two disjoint types has l1 norm at most the input norm, so the Hilbert input map is contractive. At a suffix at most one coordinate from each family is evaluated, giving output norm at most sqrt(2) times the Hilbert norm. Factorization through a reflexive space implies weak compactness; infinitely many norm-separated Boolean derivatives imply noncompactness and nonregularity. For L_le, fixed j gives eventual zero while fixed i gives eventual one along j. If R were weakly compact at distance delta<1/2, a weakly convergent subsequence of its zero-prefix columns would have limit r with |r(1^j)|<=delta for each j. A free-ultrafilter limit along 1^j is a bounded functional with values at least 1-delta on every such column and thus on r, a contradiction. The midpoint gives the matching upper bound. The prior approximation numbers apply to both nonregular languages. The original general gap is also correct: weak convergence in C(beta J) allows pointwise continuous thresholding and dominated convergence against each regular measure on a common norm bound; Eberlein–Šmulian then gives relative weak compactness of the thresholded column set and Krein's theorem gives that of its closed absolutely convex hull. No finite truncation, numerical assertion or computation is used to prove these infinite statements.

evidence: Hristov et al. prove regularity iff norm compactness and give the compact and finite-rank distance and flat approximation-number tail for every nonregular language. Section 8 does not obtain the arbitrary-injection Hilbert factorization.
The Grothendieck criterion treats all bounded families in C(K) and explains the classical weak-compactness gap and half-graph obstruction; it does not supply the structural factorization here.
The same-day palindrome result concerns length-weighted complex operators on l2 and Schatten behavior, not the real l1 to l-infinity operators and their factorizations.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The universal approximation theorem fully covers both numerical tails. Neither it nor the classical criterion provides the quantitative Hilbert maps; those require the particular derivative support structure.

evidence: Given delta<1/2, choose a continuous threshold constant 0 on (-infinity,delta] and 1 on [1-delta,infinity). Applying it to weakly compact columns in C(beta J) preserves relative weak compactness by pointwise weak sequential convergence and dominated convergence; the column hull then gives weak compactness of the Boolean operator itself. Together with the midpoint, this implies the general gap.

A classical half-graph directly gives the order-language obstruction. The Hilbert factorization of L_f uses a new ingredient relative to the inspected sources: the derivative supports for every arbitrary injection split into two disjoint families after collapsing repeated singleton supports, with a uniform bound sqrt(2).

originality.rationale: The frozen general-gap novelty claim does not pass: the midpoint together with classical weak compactness under continuous thresholding and the column hull criterion already yields the exact Boolean half-gap. This is stronger than a mere suspicion of folklore; there need not be a prior paper stating the operator distance verbatim. The repair removes the general gap from the main result and retains the concrete quantitative Hilbert factorization for arbitrary injective graphs. The same-tail comparison provides the motivation; neither the approximation numbers nor the order-language obstruction are claimed as new principles. Within the inspected literature no earlier coverage of the explicit arbitrary-injection factorization and norm bound was identified.

value.rationale: The repaired result resolves a concrete question after the compact approximation-number theorem: a flat tail for nonregular languages does not decide weak compactness, even when one side is Hilbert-factorable. The positive witness is a uniform factorization for the whole natural injective-graph family, without monotonicity or computability restrictions, not merely an isolated example or a restatement of the shared tail. The familiar order pattern is a comparison witness, not a new general obstruction.
